panels.description: The mongodb_rs_members_pingMs metric measures network round-trip latency in milliseconds between the primary MongoDB node and each replica set member. Monitoring this is critical because high ping times directly impact replication lag—if members can't communicate quickly, secondary nodes fall behind, increasing data loss risk during failovers and consuming your oplog window faster.
panels.title: Replication Ping Time

panels.description: The mongodb_rs_term metric represents the current election term number in your MongoDB replica set—a monotonically increasing integer that increments each time a new primary is elected. This is crucial for monitoring because sudden increases indicate a failover event has occurred, allowing you to track replica set stability and detect unexpected primary elections. If you see the term number jumping frequently, it signals instability in your cluster (network partitions, node failures, or configuration issues). You should alert on term changes to immediately investigate failovers, and correlate term increases with other metrics like oplog window consumption and replication lag to understand the health impact. A stable replica set maintains the same term number for extended periods, while frequent term changes indicate reliability problems requiring urgent attention
panels.title: Replica Set Term (Elections)

panels.description: Measures the MongoDB oplog window in seconds - the time span of replication history available for replica set members to catch up if they fall behind. Critical for Itential's high-availability architecture as it determines how long a secondary can be offline or lagging before requiring a full resync. Typical healthy value is 4+ hours; values below 2 hours indicate potential replication risk.
panels.title: Oplog Window

panels.description: The rate at which common DB commands are failing
panels.title: Command Failures

panels.description: Tracks the rate of write operations (inserts, updates, deletes) per hour. High write rates consume oplog space faster, reducing your oplog window. For Itential, spikes in this metric during heavy workflow execution indicate increased oplog pressure.
panels.title: Oplog Growth Rate (Bytes per Hour)

panels.description: Tracks maximum available connections, currently open connections, and actively executing connections. Exhausting available connections prevents new clients from connecting. High active counts suggest slow queries holding connections. Thresholds: Warning if current > 80% of available; Critical if > 95%; Alert if active connections > 50% of current for sustained periods.
panels.title: Active Client Connections

panels.description: Operations per second by type, showing your workload profile. Sudden spikes indicate application changes or issues; sustained high rates consume resources and oplog space faster. Important for capacity planning and detecting abnormal application behavior. Thresholds: Establish baseline for your workload; Alert on > 200% of normal baseline; Track write operations specifically as they impact oplog consumption.
panels.title: Operations Per Second

panels.description: Number of operations currently waiting in the ingress queue for execution tickets. High or sustained queue lengths indicate slow queries holding execution tickets, causing new operations to back up. Values consistently above 10 suggest performance issues requiring investigation. A healthy system typically shows 0-5 queued operations.
panels.title: MongoDB Operations Queue Length

panels.description: Operations waiting for global locks. High counts indicate contention from slow queries blocking resources. Differs from ingress queue—this is specifically lock-related blocking. Thresholds: Warning if total > 5; Critical if > 10; Alert separately on readers vs writers to identify read or write-heavy contention.
panels.title: Global Lock Queue

panels.description: Currently executing operations holding locks. High sustained counts suggest many concurrent slow operations. Useful for understanding concurrency patterns and identifying when you're hitting concurrency limits. Thresholds: Establish baseline; Alert if readers or writers > 150% of normal baseline indicating unusual concurrency or slow operations.
panels.title: Queued Operations

panels.description: Average operation latency in microseconds. High latencies indicate slow queries, resource contention, or insufficient indexes. Directly impacts application response times and user experience. Thresholds: Warning if reads > 50000µs (50ms); Critical if > 100000µs (100ms); Warning if writes > 100000µs (100ms); Critical if > 500000µs (500ms).
panels.title: Operation Latency (Average)

panels.description: Ratio of documents examined vs. returned. High ratios indicate missing indexes or inefficient queries scanning more data than necessary. Impacts query performance and resource utilization. Thresholds: Warning if ratio > 5:1 (scanning 5x more than returning); Critical if > 10:1; Optimal is close to 1:1 with proper indexes.
panels.title: Document Scanned vs Returned Ratio

panels.description: Ratio of documents examined vs. returned. High ratios indicate missing indexes or inefficient queries scanning more data than necessary. Impacts query performance and resource utilization. Thresholds: Warning if ratio > 5:1 (scanning 5x more than returning); Critical if > 10:1; Optimal is close to 1:1 with proper indexes.
panels.title: Documents Scanned vs Returned

panels.description: Number of open cursors. Sudden spikes indicate queries not being properly closed or very slow aggregations. High counts consume memory and can indicate application cursor leaks. Thresholds: Warning if total > 5000; Critical if > 10000; Alert on sustained increases indicating cursor leak; Monitor pinned cursors separately as they hold resources.
panels.title: Open Cursors

panels.description:
Current WiredTiger cache usage. Cache should be well-utilized but not constantly full (which causes excessive evictions). Low utilization may indicate working set fits in cache; consistently at maximum indicates you may need more memory. Thresholds: Monitor as percentage of max; Warning if > 85% of maximum; Critical if > 95%; combined with high eviction rates indicates memory pressure.

Amount of modified data in cache not yet written to disk. High dirty cache during heavy write workloads is normal, but if it stays near maximum, checkpoints may struggle to keep up. Thresholds: Warning if > 50% of total cache; Critical if > 75%; Combined with checkpoint delays indicates write performance issues.
panels.title: WiredTiger Cache Usage

panels.description: Rate of cache evictions. Some eviction is normal as working set changes, but high sustained eviction rates indicate cache is too small for your working set. Impacts performance as queries hit disk instead of cache. Thresholds: Monitor rate; Warning if evicting > 1000 pages/sec sustained; Critical if > 5000 pages/sec; Investigate if modified page evictions are high (indicates writes overwhelming cache).
panels.title: Cache Evictions

panels.description: Memory usage in MB. Resident is actual RAM used; virtual includes memory-mapped files. Resident growing to system limits causes OOM kills. Important for capacity planning and detecting memory leaks. Thresholds: Warning if resident > 80% of available system RAM; Critical if > 90%; Alert on unexpected growth patterns indicating potential memory leaks.
panels.title: Memory Usage

panels.description: Rate of page faults indicating working set exceeds available memory, causing disk I/O. High page faults severely degrade performance. Critical indicator that you need more RAM or have inefficient queries. Thresholds: Warning if > 10 page faults/sec; Critical if > 100 page faults/sec; Sustained page faults indicate memory pressure requiring immediate attention.
panels.title: Page Faults

panels.description: Disk space of `/var/lib/mongo`, used vs available.
panels.title: Disk Space

panels.description: Total data size per database in bytes. Tracks database growth for capacity planning. Sudden increases may indicate data ingestion issues or lack of cleanup. Important for predicting when you'll need additional storage. Thresholds: Set based on available disk space; Warning at 70% capacity; Critical at 85%; Monitor growth rate to predict capacity exhaustion.
panels.title: Database Data Size

panels.description: The percentage of disk space consumed over time.
panels.title: Data Space Used Percentage

panels.description: Total index size per database. Large indexes impact memory usage and performance. Index size should be proportional to data size; disproportionate index size may indicate unnecessary indexes. Thresholds: Monitor ratio to data size; Investigate if indexes > 50% of data size; Alert on unexpected growth indicating runaway index creation.
panels.title: Database Index Size

panels.description: Individual collection and index sizes. Allows identifying which collections are growing fastest and consuming most space. Critical for Itential's job_data.chunks and job_output collections which can grow quickly. Thresholds: Track top 10 collections; Alert if any collection growing > 10GB/day unexpectedly; Monitor index sizes relative to data.
panels.title: Collection Count

panels.description: Disk I/O operations per second. High reads with page faults indicate working set > cache. High writes during heavy workloads are normal but sustained high I/O may indicate suboptimal queries or insufficient cache. Thresholds: Establish baseline; Warning if > 200% of normal; Critical if approaching disk IOPS limits; Combine with latency metrics to detect I/O bottlenecks.
panels.title: Disk IOPS

panels.description: I/O Wait Percentage
panels.title: I/O Wait Percentage

panels.description: Transaction lifecycle metrics showing starts, commits, and rollbacks. High rollback rates indicate application errors, conflicts, or timeout issues. Important for understanding transaction health. Thresholds: Monitor rollback rate; Warning if rollbacks > 5% of commits; Critical if > 10%; Investigate causes of high rollback rates.
panels.title: Transactions

panels.description: Write conflicts when multiple transactions attempt to modify same documents. High conflicts indicate contention hotspots requiring application changes (like sharding hot documents). Impacts throughput and latency. Thresholds: Warning if > 1% of write operations encounter conflicts; Critical if > 5%; Sustained conflicts require application-level changes.
panels.title: Write Conflicts

panels.description: Number of active WiredTiger sessions. Each operation uses a session. Very high counts may indicate session leaks or unusual concurrency. Useful for understanding resource utilization. Thresholds: Monitor trends; Warning if > 1000 sessions; Critical if > 5000; Alert on sudden spikes indicating unusual activity or session leaks.
panels.title: WiredTiger Sessions

panels.description: Checkpoint duration and failures. Checkpoints write dirty data to disk—long checkpoints or failures indicate I/O bottlenecks or excessive dirty data. Failed checkpoints are critical as they prevent proper data durability. Thresholds: Warning if checkpoint > 3000ms (3 sec); Critical if > 5000ms (5 sec); Alert immediately on any failed checkpoints; Monitor max time to catch occasional spikes.
panels.title: Checkpoint stats

panels.description: Network throughput in bytes per second. Sudden increases may indicate data export jobs, index builds, or application issues. High outbound traffic suggests large result sets. Important for network capacity planning. Thresholds: Establish baseline; Warning if > 200% of normal; Monitor during maintenance windows; Alert if approaching network interface limits.
panels.title: Network Throughput

panels.description: Server assertions by type (regular, warning, msg, user, rollovers). Any asserts indicate internal MongoDB errors or warnings. Regular asserts are serious and may indicate bugs or data corruption. Thresholds: Critical alert on ANY regular asserts; Warning on msg/warning asserts; Investigate all assert increases; user asserts may indicate application issues.
panels.title: Asserts
